text:
anna-sales: Quick: NovusHealth POC request. They want Redwood Private in their AWS account. Requirements: egress through their TLS-inspect proxy, SOC needs original client IPs in request logs, and they need a tiny static allowlist for change window. Can we do this without huge ops work?

diego-netops: Yes. Two practical topologies with tradeoffs:
1) PrivateLink (interface endpoint) -> Redwood-managed connector: easiest for customer ops but ENI IPs are ephemeral. If their proxy inspects TLS and SNATs, we will only see proxy IP unless proxy forwards X-Forwarded-For.
2) Connector deployed in-customer VPC (NLB w/ EIPs): preferred for audit requirements. Use NLB TCP passthrough to preserve client IP at TCP layer; allocate 2 EIPs for HA and provide those for firewall allowlist.

hannah-se: Note on TLS/mTLS: if you want mutual TLS between client and connector, terminate on connector and validate client certs; if proxy performs TLS inspect and re-terminates, configure proxy to inject X-Forwarded-For and avoid SNAT when possible.

kyle-ps: Procurement question: which option shows lower immediate AWS charges for them?

diego-netops: PrivateLink has AWS endpoint hourly + per-GB processing costs. Connector-in-VPC means they pay EC2/NLB/EIP costs but gives stable IPs. For a short POC we recommend connector-in-VPC and we often offer a POC infra credit.

anna-sales: They need a pasteable firewall ticket for this week's change window (two variants).

diego-netops: Paste these. Variant A (Connector-in-VPC, recommended):
```
Allow TCP/443 from App Subnet 10.30.0.0/22 to Connector NLB EIPs 198.51.100.45 and 198.51.100.46 (outbound)
Allow TCP/443 from Connector NLB EIPs to App ALB SG for callback/inbound flows
```
Variant B (PrivateLink):
```
Allow TCP/443 from App Subnet 10.30.0.0/22 to Interface Endpoint ENI IPs (ENIs will be provided post-creation). Note: ENI IPs may change if endpoint is re-created; request re-validation after endpoint changes.
```

kyle-ps: Can we also provide the short SIEM/logging note?

hannah-se: One-liner: "Connector emits a per-request UUID (request_id) and includes X-Request-Id in responses. We can forward logs to your TLS Syslog endpoint or S3. To preserve client IPs include X-Forwarded-For from your proxy or use NLB TCP passthrough."

deploy-bot: Created ephemeral POC connector stack in acct 098765432101 (us-east-2). id: poc-novus-122. NLB provisioned, awaiting EIP assignment.

anna-sales: Owners: diego -> final allowlist + 1-page runbook (EOD tomorrow); hannah -> security answers for mTLS/KMS/log-forwarding; kyle -> add POC credit blurb to quote. I'll schedule handoff call. Thanks everyone.

diego-netops: I'll include sample SG/iptables snippets and the exact proxy header snippet to request from their proxy team.

anna-sales: Perfect ":"
